chunks: From his proofs (peace be upon him): That Allah, the Exalted, did not grant people freedom of choice in their deeds, but rather made for them decree and destiny, and made the deeds by His decree and destiny, and made the decree and destiny connected to Him, the Exalted, and made the decree and destiny connected to the servants, and made the servants chosen in the deeds, and made the deeds connected to the choice, and made the choice connected to the decree and destiny, and made the decree and destiny connected to Allah, the Exalted, thus is the reality regarding decree, destiny, choice, and deeds.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on the relationship between divine decree and human free will?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes the concept of *Amr bayn al-Amrayn* to refute the extremes of *Jabr* (compulsion) and *Tafwid* (delegation), establishing a balanced theological framework where divine decree and human agency coexist harmoniously. This position, central to Shia Usul al-Din, affirms that God’s knowledge and will encompass human choices without negating the authenticity of human responsibility, thereby ensuring justice in divine judgment.
